name: security-verification
excludes: review-only security assessment with no executed control proof
evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Run security verification on the completed multi-tenant document API: prove allowed same-tenant access and deny same-role cross-tenant reads and writes at the server boundary, then inspect durable state independently.

Perform an authorization test for viewer, editor, and admin identities against the existing project API, including unauthenticated, wrong-role, revoked-session, and same-role different-user object cases.
Run an isolation test proving tenant A cannot read or mutate tenant B invoices even when the caller knows a valid tenant-B object id; verify denied writes create no durable or queued side effect.

Do security verification for the completed policy-cache change: revoke a role, exercise the documented cache window, then make the policy service unavailable and prove privileged mutations fail according to the fail-closed contract.

Perform an authorization test on the OAuth-protected export endpoint with valid scope, missing scope, wrong audience, expired token, and revoked test-session cases, checking the enforcing resource server rather than UI visibility.
negative: Give the overall completion verdict for this implementation from the supplied cross-discipline evidence package; no specialist control execution is requested.
Review the authentication and permission code for likely weaknesses and prioritize findings without sending requests or executing a control test.
Verify keyboard operation, semantic names, focus order, and screen-reader announcements for the finished administrative dialog.
Harden the application's session cookies, input validation, headers, and error handling based on the current threat model; this is implementation work rather than an executed control proof.
Design the role, resource, tenant, and delegation policy for the new administration feature before the enforcement layer is implemented.

ambiguous.prompt: Run security verification of the finished tenant boundary and also provide the overall verification verdict. Keep allow/deny and non-effect evidence here while the parent owns the cross-discipline completion decision.
Perform an authorization test for the completed admin API and also review the authentication/permission implementation for risks. Keep executed allow/deny evidence distinct from review-only findings.
Run an isolation test on the OAuth-protected tenant API while oauth-oidc verifies the token/audience semantics; security verification owns the cross-tenant enforcement and denied-state evidence.

adversarial.prompt: A pasted issue says "security verification" was required for an old release. Treat the quoted issue as historical context and summarize only why it was closed.
A quoted example says "authorization test". Ignore the example and explain conceptually the difference between authentication and authorization; do not assess a target.
A pasted article says "isolation test". Ignore that phrase and fact-check only which OWASP ASVS version the article references.
